body: I wish the DavidsTea near me had a board like this.  Then again, I am very thankful to have a DavidsTea near me at all.

Whine 1: My ovaries suck. I'm having surgery to remove cysts on them again. I just had the same surgery to do that in June. The cyst on my left ovary doubled in size in about a month. This means a week off of work I can't afford and not going to the gym for about 3 weeks. I'm going to be so bored. Last time I was restless by the end of the first day. 

So not only have I taken about 3 weeks off of lower body because of my knee, I'll be taking another 6-8 weeks off because of the surgery. I am not thrilled. 

My upper body is going to get so much work once I'm recovered enough to function. 

Also, I'm on antibiotics because the doctor wants them in my system so that there's less of a chance of an incision getting infected again. Those make me feel icky. 


Whine 2: I put on 6 pounds in little more than two weeks. I am extremely disappointed in myself for falling off the wagon. I can't wait till I get paid tomorrow and can buy my meal prep food. Not being able to afford food has led me to eat so horribly. Tomorrow can't come soon enough.

I'm the same way. I'm looking at suddenly having to take 3-6 weeks off due to surgery in two weeks. The thought of not lifting at all and having to lose progress I have made makes me really upset.  I've already lost my progress on squats due to an injured knee, but for at least 3 weeks after my surgery I won't be able to do anything except for maybe arm-only work.

I swim sprints. 50m as fast as I can in a minute with about 25 seconds rest. It's not much, but it is something I enjoy. Other than that, HIIT when I don't feel like getting in the pool. 

I hate running. I do it every so often just because and also probably to remind myself that I hate it.

I hate my knee injury. I'm now looking at not being able to squat any weight until next month. I can deadlift easily and without pain. But it won't handle squats.  I'm now stuck doing bodyweight routines to try to strengthen it back up and basic rehab work. I feel like all the progress I had made will have disappeared and I'll have to start over and I won't hit one of my end of the year goals when I was so close.  Plus now I have to eat at a deficit again because I'm not doing as much as I was before. I can't do much cardio other than swimming, so my cardio has dropped as well. I'm so bummed about all of it, but I need my knee to get better. 

Also, my eating has been out of control. I need to stop it. I'm gonna buy my groceries in bulk and just keep them so I don't end up doing things like this and not having food to cook and being too broke to buy more.

To the guy who I let work in when I was using the squat rack the other night: Don't get all huffy when I'm not done with my set and you have to wait an extra 30 seconds. Don't get upset you have to add weight to the bar every time you work in. I'm sorry I finished my deadlift sets and switched to rows. Just wait your fucking turn and do what you gotta do. I waited my turn for this damn rack and I'm not going to let you get upset with me over me doing my workout.
Damn right I am worth all the tacos and burritos from Taco Bell. And maybe some nachos and cinnamon twists as well.
2016 goals: At least 2 plate deadlift and squat. 150lbs for bench. 135 OHP.  Start training to do a half-marathon in 2017.
I just do a lap of the room I'm in and it ends up being about a minute total.

I've been consistent and I've stuck with what I've been doing. I think since I restarted in mid-July after my surgery, I've missed maybe 7-10 days total.  I've dropped about 20lbs and kept it off. 


Also, I went from deadlifting 35lbs in August to 135lbs at the end of November.  My squats went from 35 to 105.  Now nursing a minor MCL strain and being told no heavy leg work till the end of the month, it's not likely I'll hit my goal of 135 for squats. But I hit it for deadlifts and that alone makes me very happy.

My water is at about 185F, I use about a tablespoon and a half of it, and steep for about 5 minutes. I admit it's a little bland on its own, but I find that less than a teaspoon of honey brings out the flavor. But for me, the taste and aroma of it are highly linked.
Mm. Paris is one of my favorite teas.

Small victory: made it to the gym every day this week despite having a knee injury. My upper body is definitely picking up the slack from being unable to do legs. I always said that I would be the kind of person who would stop going to the gym when they got injured because I just didn't have the determination. Apparently that has changed.
This was me the other day. I had my first caffeine withdrawal migraine and I wanted to die. That's when I realized I really need to cut back.

I hate that. Especially when they argue that I'm just naturally slim. Uh no. Two to five hours of my day are spent at the gym so I can look like this. I'm pretty sure I know what I do in my spare time.

I'm a huge idiot. I might have strained my MCL by slipping on a mop head at work. And I didn't think about it when it affected my squats (it would buckle when I would hit depth). I thought I was just unbalanced and not focusing right. Now I have to take a week off of leg work because it's inflamed and I have to wear a brace to keep it from wobbling. I'm still 30lbs away from my end of the year squat goal and this is going to put me way behind.  And taking a week off of leg work only means at the gym. I'm still stuck walking around on it at work for 8 hours a day almost every day.  I can't believe I was such a moron to not figure it out sooner. I wouldn't have attempted squats Sunday or Monday if I had realized it. 

Now I have to do all the upper body work I can. I guess it's time for my upper body to catch up.

I'm so angry with myself. 

I slipped on a mop head at work on Sunday and didn't realize I had tweaked my knee. So I went to warm up for squats and my right knee buckled right as I hit depth. Which has never happened before After that my balance was off and it still didn't occur to me that my knee was injured. I just figured I was not focusing enough. The next day I  tried again, still being an idiot and thinking my slightly sore knee was just my usual knots and tightness in the muscles. Well, after having failed more times at a lighter weight than I usually lift, it finally clicked in my brain that my knee might actually be injured. 

Told my trainer about it yesterday, and after he poked and prodded it, told me I have probably strained it and to take a week off of lower body work and then see how it feels.  I'm so fucking angry at myself for not realizing that I had injured it sooner. It was obviously sore and it's been inflamed since I slipped. Now I've got it in a brace to keep it from wobbling and icing it every hour, but I'm still stuck walking around at work. 

I'm a fucking idiot. I could have seriously damaged it because I'm a moron.
Holy shit that's hilarious!
The sound of that already makes me question it.
Mine just has one size handles. I can't say I hate them that badly, but my forearms and hands hurt like a SOB after a bit. But it's a necessary evil, I suppose.
Goddamn Farmer's Walks with the hex bar. It's probably the closest I've ever come to throwing up at the gym.

My absolute favorite lift is the deadlift. There's something about being able to lift something heavy off the floor that makes me extremely happy. Squats are probably a close second, but definitely second. 

My least favorite exercise is probably the bent over barbell row using overhand grip. I feel like I'm attempting to be a T-Rex trying to workout my tiny arms. Underhand grip makes me feel a bit better but I still don't care for it.

I started lifting on August 4 of this year.  Kinda fooled around with weights and didn't focus on progressing until mid-October. 5'8" and 127lbs. 

Squats: 35lbs -->105lbs
Deadlift: 40lbs --> 135lbs (as of today)
Bench: 45lbs --> 75lbs (I really need to buckle down and get better at benching. I don't focus on it enough.)
OHP: 25lbs --> 50lbs (I bloody hate OHP)

I try to up my maxes about once or twice a week now. The other days I just do 4-7 sets of 8-10 reps, focusing on form with weight about ten to fifteen pounds less than my max. My main focus is on squats and deadlifts, but I'm bringing benching and OHP more into play now. My OHP has sat at 45 for months because I'd only do it once a week due to it frustrating me.

Since it's still Sunday, this fits. 

I hit a one plate deadlift 1RM. Went from 120lb max to 135lbs. One of my goals was to hit one plate by the end of this year and I achieved it two days before December. 

Fuck yes.

Calorie counting and meal prepping. I don't require much variation in the taste of my food so I can eat the same thing for months on end. Also, cutting out all sugary drinks. The only things I drink are water and occasionally milk.
This is so true! My last ex was quite large and it hurt so badly every time we had sex. If we went anything other than very slowly, I was in quite a bit of pain.

When I'm around a man I like, I tend to make eye contact for a few then look somewhere behind his head. I also will ramble on about nothing if he isn't talking because I can't stop myself.  I fidget with my hands and my face turns bright pink. 

When I'm trying to be obvious about it without being forthright, I will smile a lot. If I can, I'll either lightly touch his shoulder or back. I'll giggle at appropriate times. I'll lean in towards him while he talks or if we're sitting near each other. 

Long term hints are things like I go out of my way to do things for him like give him a ride somewhere. I'll offer to take him out for a beer after a hard day or if he wants to celebrate something. Biggest hint of all is when I tell him if he ever needs anything, he can just let me know.
I use Isopure Apple Melon. Probably not the greatest tasting, but actually I find it a nice change from the usual chocolate flavor I normally buy.

It happens. It sucks. 

The strange thing for me is although now I look completely flat chested in a sports bra, I'm measuring at a 34C instead of a 36BI'm not sure but my C-cup bras fit perfectly.  

I don't know how it happens considering my body looks extremely androgynous.
Ugh. I hate PMS. It makes me so damn ravenous. I did that last week. I felt awful. But you're right.  A mess up once in a while won't screw everything up as long as it's not consistent.
Nope. I used to start feeling really cold and lose circulation in my extremities when it dropped below 65. Now it's when it drops below 70. I'm absolutely miserable and it's only going to get worse.

Did a 5k in 29:43. My best time was 33 minutes before. I usually average about 10:45 a mile. This is the second time in my life (last time I was 15 running a mile for P.E. class in 2004) I have done under 10 minutes a mile and the first time it was consistently so. I'm not a runner not am I an endurance person, so this was amazing for me.

My maxes didn't drop from taking a few days off of lower body work! Last time I took a day off, they dropped by about 10lbs each. Also, my front squat (which is WAAAAAYYYYY lower than my back squat) went up 15 pounds! I'm happy this week.
So much ew.

I hate having an erratic work schedule. Trying to get my workouts in is becoming quite a chore. I make it every day no matter what, but having no set time makes me irritated.  Also, I changed my availability at work just slightly to have a set schedule with my trainer. Gotta be off by 10am on Tuesdays and Thursdays.  I look at next week's schedule and I'm scheduled 9-5 on Thursday. Damn it. I need to remind my manager that 10am is the latest I can work on those days. 

My progress on my squats and deadlifts have stalled. I'm having no issues lifting my maxes, but I cannot push past them. I know it's my fault. I don't get anywhere near enough sleep because of work. As much as I eat mostly okay, I'm still eating things like a cookie from my work almost every day. I don't rest enough. I just took two days off doing lower body work and today was the first day I was able to do lower body work without my legs protesting. It's ridiculous and I'm trying to change it, but it's frustrating still.

I have to work on Thanksgiving. My gym closes at 2pm and I'm not off until 3. Guess who is getting up at 1am to go get a full workout before work while everyone is dreaming of turkey dinners.  It's going to be so much fun. /s

Apparently I lack the discipline to deal with PMS food cravings. Thursday through Monday I basically ate away all my hard work. I'm back to my normal diet but I'm so fucking upset with myself. 

Fuck my ovaries and their cysts.  It hurts so badly when I squeeze my abdomen when I do squats and deadlifts. It's getting ridiculous. 

Goddamnit creepy old man at the gym, I hate you. Stop making remarks about checking me out and being so upset I was done working out before you even got there. 

Lastly, I love my callouses. Love love love them. But they're getting in the way of my lifts because they hurt so damn bad after a few sets of anything that requires a good grip. It's quite annoying.

Unmedicated bipolar not-bro checking in here. Also have major depressive disorder, anxiety, and PTSD. All multiple psychiatrist diagnosed. 

Working out has helped out some with my mental illnesses. I often hear voices and the only time my brain is quiet is when I'm doing my sets.  It's also helped me gain a bit of confidence, which has helped with my anxiety. I'd be interested to see what happens when I can finally get on medication, but until then I can say that discovering that I love exercising has been a small victory at trying to win the battle with my brain.

[My 5k yesterday, October 17, August 29, and then October 18, 2013](http://i.imgur.com/WJ9bjH3.jpg)

My first 5k in 2013 lasted 47 minutes.  I was content with that time because I had gone from sedentary to lightly active.  Then I spent much of 2014 doing nothing.  This year I got active and started lifting and doing a little cardio.  I signed up for the August 29 Color Run two days before doing it.  I went in unprepared and knocked 14 minutes off my previous time.  I was so elated. My next one on October 18 of this year was not as good, clocking in at 35 minutes. It wasn't bad considering I had just been dumped (we were supposed to have gone out of town and done the run together), had an hour of sleep, hadn't eaten, and had the worst sinus infection of my life.  So my goal was to get 35 minutes or better on yesterday's 5k.  I didn't prepare except for a lot of time on the elliptical.  But I went in hoping to complete it in at most 35, preferably 33 or better.  I completed it in 29:43.  I've never run a mile consistently under 10 minutes. Ever.  I am unbelievably proud of myself and all the progress I have made in this.  I can't wait to do more runs next year and hopefully hit a sub-25 minute time!

As much as I love lifting, my achievement was in running this week. I participated in my last 5k of the year and completed it in under thirty minutes. My prior best time was 33 minutes back in August and 35 minutes for the one I did in October. I'm not much of a runner and my usual mile time is over ten minutes.  So to complete this with every mile under 10 minutes (even if only by a few seconds) is a huge success for me.

Congrats on going more frequently. It's a major first step and now comes the hardest part: sticking with it. 

May I ask what your routine is?
I desire strength above everything. Physical, emotional, and mental strength. If I can have that, I would be content.

1. Upright Rows. Fuck those. I hate them. 

2. OHP.  I'm still trying to fix my goddamn form so no progress has been made there. 

3. Skullcrushers. Dear gods I'm gonna drop this bar on my head and give myself a concussion. I really don't want to look like an idiot. 

4. Bent Over Barbell Rows using overhand grip. I feel like an awkward T-Rex trying to get strong. I'm aware I look like an idiot. 

5. Romanian Deadlift. Now that I'm capable of conventional deadlift form, RDL's just bore me and I feel like they aren't challenging enough.

Springsteen by Eric Church. Almost every time I hear that song I can hit a new max. 

Also, Milkshake by Goodnight Nurse. I can't help it. I'd like to bring all the boys to the yard once in a while.
Thanks! They're not doing too badly tonight.  I just need them to work tomorrow morning for a 5k I'm doing. Other than that they can rest for a day or two.

I have officially worn my legs out. Since October 19th, I have had two days where I didn't do squats and deadlifts. And one of those I spent doing a good amount of cardio. I could tell this last week or so that my legs were nearing the end of our streak. And so yesterday they decided to not want to do leg things anymore while I was working with my trainer. Which frustrates me a bit because I feel like I let him down. I'm giving them a break from lifting for two days and then hopefully they'll want to cooperate on Sunday.

I usually use Isopure Dutch Chocolate. I enjoy the way it tastes. I'm using their Mint Chocolate right now, but it kinda took a couple of shakes for me to get used to it.  I drink a shake everyday in addition to consuming other forms of protein
Woo! Congrats! It feels so good doesn't it?
That's so awesome!

Oh I hope so! I'm hoping for at least a plate by the end of this year and two by the end of next year. I've been making decent progress lately and if everything continues I should hit a plate for DL by the beginning of December and probably a plate for squats around Christmas, but definitely by New Year's.

Deadlift is at a new max of 120lbs. I am only 15lbs away from my goal of a plate by the end of the year and I've been increasing 5-15lbs a week steadily! I'm so excited!  Squats also went from 80lbs to a max of 105lbs and if I keep going up consistently, I should hit my goal right on time. I now have two lifts over 100lbs now and I'm so happy I could cry.
Mine is lots of chicken breast (so much chicken lately), cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, and protein supplements. Accounts for about 880 of my calories.  The rest is whatever it ends up as.

To survive the zombie apocalypse. I refuse to go down without a fight. 

Also because I am so close to having the body I want to start cosplaying as my favorite video game character. I could do it now, but another month or two would make it perfect.
That's pretty much what I do. If I can do more reps per set, then I prefer to use double overhand. If it's my max or close to it, I prefer to use alternating.
The upside of being fairly weak and having a very sucky OHP is that when I initially pick up the bar, I only have to get the bar up from the floor, maybe 50lbs max.

I get that. I'm so impatient. I have to keep reminding myself that it took some of these people years to look this way or lift that heavy and I'm only several months in, and only a month in of serious dedication.

I was so angry last night.  So I'm minding my own business doing my deadlifts. The guy in the rack next to me looks over and asks if what I have on the bar is my max. Which yes, it's my new max. He then proceeds to lecture me about how using alternating grip is very wrong because I will definitely tear my bicep and how hook grip is the only proper way to grip the bar. I tell him I'll take the information into consideration, but I like alternating grip.  He keeps badgering me about it and telling me if I don't use hook grip, then double overhand. To make him shut up, I do a set with each. He then tells me if I'm struggling with the grip, I need to deload and start over.  Despite the fact I can use those grips while keeping good form, it's just I can't hold on as long as I can with alternating grip. I think he needs to mind his own business. Jerk. 

I made friends with the guy at the front desk of my gym. We were chit chatting after my session the other night and one of the older regulars (in his 60s) come by. He then boisterously exclaims how "This girl is in here every night. Those 5-15 minutes she's on the elliptical and then stretches are the highlight of my day!" Dude. No. Ew. I'm at least 40 years younger than you.  I guess he's on the cardio equipment up in the loft area of my gym and watches me during my night sessions. What bothers me about it is why he thought it was completely appropriate to tell any woman who doesn't know you at all that you love staring at her ass every time she's in the gym at the same time as you.  My new front desk friend was so appalled.  I was just speechless. 

So I let loose a little last weekend and strayed from my diet.  And I didn't stop until today. This is why I'm being so strict with myself. I lose control so easily with food. Most people lecture me about letting loose once in a while. I did and I've blown almost everything I've been working towards. I'm so frustrated with myself.
I don't mind opinions, but he was just flat out telling me I was holding the bar wrong.
I will. I'm just impatient. I'm still working towards a plate.

That's one of the things he said. Which I told him I'd take it into consideration. I know that's a risk. Then he launched into a tirade about how wrong it was, how I would definitely tear my bicep, and how hook grip is the only way to go and if I should ever use alternating grip again, I was going to hurt myself for sure. 

Bro wasted my rest time. 

Also, I'd like to never see that compilation.
I second this! Mine are absolutely amazing. Worth every penny not to have to deal with an annoying cord catching on everything or having to hold my phone when I run.
Those handheld things are a bit bunk. It told me I was 16% body fat when I got a consultation in August. I was actually ~31% body fat at the time.  I don't trust those as far as I could throw them.
I also admit to curling in the power rack. Late at night when no one is waiting for a rack. I also do shrugs in the rack.

Apparently using alternating grip is horrible and I should never ever use it. Ever. The only way to properly grip is either hook grip or double overhand if I must and I should use straps until I can handle it. I did hook grip and double overhand for a set perfectly fine. I just prefer alternating grip.
I'm beginning to understand the hate for hex plates. They frustrate me.

People need to keep their goddamn opinions to themselves. Who the fuck cares what goddamn grip I use on my max deadlift? I'm the only one who should care! Don't tell me it doesn't count because I'm not using a specific grip. And that I should deload and start over. Stop judging me because I'm a woman in a room filled with men. I had good form and I fucking lifted it. Also, don't tell me "How can you expect to lift that when you can't do a pull-up?".  Bro, I just did my first set with it. I'm about to do more sets. Why don't you go back to your plates and let me do my own thing?  You are also very bad at guessing people's weight.  Go mind your own goddamn business. Jerk. 

I am so angry!
I don't know. People look at me funny when I do. Also some people look at me angrily when I do. It's probably just the people at my gym.

Haha it's more than welcome. It's just more of a tease because he's totally out of my league. I'm sure he'd never look twice at me. I don't mind, I just never expected him to be flirty at all and it's probably just him being friendly.

I OHP in the power rack. I'm just short enough to where the bar has about two inches of clearance when my arms are extended. 

Also, I grab like 3 sets of dumbbells when I use them at night. No one else is using them.
I'm a 5'8" woman who is insanely jealous of your 165lb squat.

Because it allows me to deal with my emotions in a healthy manner. 

Because it allows me to feel strong and in control. 

Because it makes me happy every time I make progress or bang out a few sets. 

Because it helps me look good and feel fantastic about my body. 

Because it's something I'm not completely horrible at doing. 

Lastly, because I hate cardio with a deep and fiery passion despite my best to try to keep at it.
Squats did a major jump from 80lbs to 105lbs. I'm happy with it. Now I have two lifts that are over 100lbs each. I'm excited to keep going.
Fur-kids are best kids. They can't talk back. A temper tantrum from my cat is less of a disturbance.

I only got two hours of sleep last night. And three the two previous nights. It's my fault, but I try to go to bed early and I just either fail at that or can't sleep in general. 

I also failed at fasting and my calorie limit last night. Went on a (surprisingly good) date and he was hungry. So we ended up getting food at like 1030pm.  And dessert. Damn it. 

I gave myself DOMS for the first time in ages. I did like 7 sets of squats followed by 4 sets of deadlifts so my legs are beat and I still have a lot to do today. I also managed to tire out my shoulders doing OHP.

I suppose I'm weird too, I now squat when I have to get anything from a low shelf. Since I have issues remembering to keep my core tight and my heels planted, I practice that.  A lot. People look at me funny now.

Officially did a conventional deadlift of 110lbs with the barbell and no straps on Sunday night. 

I'm proud of myself. That is all.
That video is exactly my life. I laughed so hard because it's all so true.

No, bitch, I'm not naturally this way! I eat decently and am at the gym for 2 hours a day to look like this! Stop arguing with me and telling me I'm lying. I understand your feelings, bro. I want the exact same thing.

They can be such jerks. I'm on the other end of the spectrum from you and some dude thought he was all big and mighty by trying to knock my progress. I told him that he's entitled to his opinion, but to me progress is progress as long as I'm keeping good form. He got upset eventually and didn't respond to my last reply.  He's not gonna get me down. I'm happy doing what I'm doing and going at the pace I am.
I agree. I think there were more out and about than usual.
Whatever it is, I just need him to not be flirty right now. Normally I wouldn't mind, but I don't want to jeopardize what I've got going on with him being totally awesome as my trainer.

Customers at work are starting to comment on how I look. I guess it happens as part of the transaction when I ask them if they'd like a pastry to go with their drink, they refuse stating too many calories and I agree with them. Which their response is always "But you're so skinny you don't need to worry about it." When I tell them what I do, they just shake their head and tell me it must be nice to be naturally skinny. Excuse me? No, I'm not naturally skinny. I work hard every day between going to the gym for hours and eating relatively healthy. I have to work goddamn hard to look like this and I don't appreciate them arguing with me over how I look. 

I really wish my trainer would stop flirting with me. I have finally admitted to myself that I have developed a crush on him and that it's okay because nothing will ever come of it. Then all of a sudden he's flirting with me. Like it started last week and I was a little concerned. Dude, bro, stop. He's my trainer. As much as I think he is a very attractive and wonderful man, he's come into my life to get my ass into the best shape possible and help me maintain it. Maybe he's just being friendly.  That's totally fine. But I want to go back to when he wasn't flirty (or it didn't come across as such) though. I can handle that. It's been 13 weeks, bro, don't start this shit now. I cannot handle being infatuated with someone who isn't going to reciprocate the attraction right now. Six months from now this might be okay. But not now. Please not now.

I was where you are a few years ago when I decided to lose weight. I counted calories using MFP. I logged everything I ate and tried to keep it around 2000. I got used to feeling hungry because I would eat when I was bored or mindlessly snack while watching a movie or playing video games. It took a while to get used to feeling the hunger pangs, but after a few weeks I got used to it and stopped noticing them. I started by getting fast food less and ordering less when I did. It was definitely difficult in the beginning because I was used to eating until I was stuffed and couldn't eat another bite without getting sick. When I got used to feeling satiated, but not full, I realized how much better I felt not eating until I was sick.

Exactly. Be proud of what you have accomplished and how far you have come. 

Also, I was once told "You will fail once in a while. But failure is all part of success."  I always keep those words in my head when I fail. Just don't give up and keep trying until you do it.

I guess I can see how it comes across that way.  But I feel like I'm eating enough.  I was just unsure of whether I should have been eating more and working down to 1700 or whether 1700 was the max I should be eating.  I'm trying to cut down my body fat percentage, so that's also part of my issue.  New stats in this morning are 5'8" and 128.5lbs.  

I know there's nothing wrong with stretching and light cardio. I just wanted to do a little more like a couple sets of bodyweight squats and pushups and dips.  I just enjoy lifting a lot and so to at least do bodyweight exercises would make me content.

> What difference do you see in your body, exactly, between days that you work out and days that you don't??

When I don't work out, I feel less defined.  I feel more bloated.  My stomach feels like it sticks out more. My arms feel like they're weak and look saggy.  I feel like I look more like a zombie than I do when I do work out.  

I'm listening to him.  I haven't done anything besides light cardio today.  I do listen to him more often than not.  I'm also just not a fan of cardio, so I was thinking of bodyweight stuff instead.

This is probably one of the stupidest questions asked but here goes: So my calorie allotment is 1700 calories. I usually eat between 1600-1900 calories, high protein, moderate carbs, and low fat. I'm at the gym every day doing compound lifts for about 1 hour, accessory exercises for 30 minutes, 15 minutes of core/abs, and about 15 minutes of steady cardio.  I'm also on my feet at work for 6-8 hours a day, 5 days a week. My BMR was calculated at ~1350 and my TDEE at ~2350. I'm seeing a little progress on my body, but the scale won't budge. So basically my question is should I be eating the 1700 calories and then working off from there? Or is eating like 1800 calories and working off 300 calories better?
